title: Retail sales slump in July. Cheaper gas and Amazon Prime hangover are the chief culprits.
summary: U.S. retail sales fell by the largest margin in 14 months in July, driven by lower gas station purchases due to cheaper fuel and reduced online shopping after Amazon's summer sale. The decline reflects shifting consumer spending patterns rather than economic weakness. The adjustment could signal changes in consumer behavior going forward.
content: Sales at U.S. retailers posted the largest decline in July in 14 months, but not because the economy sputtered. Americans spent less at gas stations due to cheaper fuel and bought less online after Amazon’s summer sales bonanza.
